questions.q: What is the default sort direction in a SOQL ORDER BY clause?
questions.explain: ASC is the default; ORDER BY Name and ORDER BY Name ASC return identically ordered results.

questions.q: By default, where do null values sort in SOQL unless you specify otherwise?
options: They are excluded from results entirely
questions.explain: Salesforce sorts null values first by default; use NULLS LAST to push them to the bottom of the sort instead.
questions.distractorExplain: Null values sort first by default in SOQL, not last — NULLS LAST is the keyword you'd add to override that default and push them to the bottom instead.

questions.q: In ORDER BY Industry ASC, AnnualRevenue DESC, what role does AnnualRevenue play?
options: It is ignored because only one ORDER BY field is allowed
It is the primary sort key, evaluated before Industry
It breaks ties only among rows that already share the same Industry value
It filters out rows with no revenue
questions.explain: The second field in a multi-field ORDER BY only determines order among rows tied on the first field.

questions.q: What is the documented maximum value for OFFSET in a SOQL query?
questions.explain: SOQL's OFFSET clause has a documented maximum of 2,000 rows; exceeding it raises a NUMBER_OUTSIDE_VALID_RANGE error.

questions.q: Why is OFFSET-based paging a poor strategy for systematically walking an object with hundreds of thousands of records?
options: OFFSET automatically limits results to 10 rows regardless of the LIMIT value
OFFSET requires a GROUP BY clause to function
OFFSET only works on custom objects, not standard objects
OFFSET is capped at 2,000 rows, so it cannot page through a dataset that large at all
questions.explain: Because OFFSET tops out at 2,000, it cannot be used to page arbitrarily deep into a large object — filtering on an indexed field like Id is the documented alternative for that case.
